name: European Accessibility Act
evidence_rating: ex-ante only: applies since June 2025; impact assessment forecasts
summary: The accessibility requirements apply to new products and services since 28 June 2025, so no evaluation exists yet (the Commission reports by 2030). The impact assessment estimated that common requirements would cut the cost of meeting divergent national accessibility rules by up to about half, from a baseline of around EUR 20 billion a year in 2020.

indicators.objective: Applies since 28 June 2025; first Commission report due in 2030
Lower costs of divergent national accessibility rules
indicators.indicator: Annual cost to business of accessibility requirements
indicators.target_or_baseline: baseline about EUR 20 billion (2020); savings up to 45-50% (forecast)

literature.citation: European Commission (2015), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a European Accessibility Act, SWD(2015) 264
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a European Accessibility Act
literature.headline: Baseline annual cost of around EUR 20 billion in 2020; the options considered would save 20-50% of it; firms surveyed put extra accessibility costs below 5% of production costs
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected one set of EU accessibility rules to cost firms much less than many national ones, and to widen the market for accessible products.
